sentences.text: 2. An extent of 7.80 Ares of land in Re.Survey Nos.35/21, 35/22, 35/25 and 35/14 of Panayam Village in Kollam Taluk was acquired for doubling of railway track.

Notification under Section 4(1)
was published on 13.05.1991 and possession was taken on 25.11.1994.
The Land Acquisition Collector passed award on 07.04.1995 and an initial compensation of Rs.2,77,427.90/- was granted.
Thereafter relying on the judgment in L.A.R.No.36/97, the claimant sought redetermination.
Additional compensation of Rs.3,32,935/- was granted.
The additional compensation was received under protest and application for reference was submitted.
3. In its statement, the claimant contended that the property was included in a lower category and compensation was granted at the rate of Rs.14,491.28/- per Are.
He claimed 2025:KER:84430 the centage value of Rs.30,000/- and other statutory benefits.
In L.A.R.No.36/97, land value was redetermined to Rs.14,491/- and Rs.18,113.52/- respectively with statutory benefits.
On conclusion of evidence, the court awarded additional compensation of Rs.2,22,716/- with 15% interest for excess compensation of Rs.57,525/-.

4. Heard the learned Senior Government Pleader for the appellant and also the learned counsel for the 2 nd respondent.
5.

The prime contention raised by learned Senior Government Pleader as well as the learned Standing Counsel for the 2nd respondent is that the court below was not correct in permitting the category change as the proceedings was under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act.

It is pointed State Of Kerala, Represented By The ... vs Viswanathan Pillai on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16859878/
2 out that the in a proceeding under Section 28A, permitting category change is permissible as laid down by this Court in various judgments.

sentences.text: It is submitted that an extent of 2.20 Ares of land acquired was included in category No.2 and remaining extent was included in category No.3.
Court below has now included the entire property in category No.2 and awarded 2025:KER:84430 compensation for the entire extent acquired from the claimant.
In view of the law laid down by this court in various judgments, changing of the category is not permissible under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act.
Therefore the appeal is allowed.
The impugned judgment is set aside.
No costs.

Sd/-
